newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. confirms Zaire forces to meet in Germany.
newsitem.headline: U.S. confirms Zaire forces to meet in Germany.

text.p: Countries planning to send troops to Zaire will meet in Germany on Wednesday to review the force's size and mandate now that Rwandan refugees are going home, the U.S. military confirmed on Sunday.

"A group of military planners led by the Canadians will meet in Stuttgart at the joint task force facility," U.S. Navy Captain Tim Taylor, director of public affairs for the U.S. European command based in Stuttgart, told Reuters.
Taylor said an advance team of Canadian officials had arrived in Stuttgart to plan the meeting, which is scheduled to be held at Kelly Barracks in the south German city.

"We are providing the facility for this meeting but the Canadians are leading the multi-national planning effort," said Taylor, spokesman for the U.S. military headquarters that controls U.S. forces in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

South African Deputy President Thabu Mbeki told a news conference at the World Food Summit in Rome on Sunday about the meeting, which is to be held to iron out mission details now that hundreds of thousands of refugees have begun making their way back to Rwanda.

Taylor also said a U.S. military team remained in central Africa on Sunday assessing the scope of potential U.S. involvement in the mission and the logistics of sending troops to join the planned Canadian-led peacekeeping mission.
